title: Prairie Systems activation orientation + network intake
summary: Kickoff orientation focused on activation timeline, networking/VPC requirements, and security checkpoints for a hybrid deployment. Customer prefers a private VPC with limited hosted fallbacks. Agreed to run a short pre-prod pilot targeting chat support flows; Redwood to provide network diagram, security docs, and pilot pricing by next Wednesday.
action_items: Avery Chen: Share activation runbook + pricing spreadsheet (due 2026-12-24)
Luis Ramirez: Schedule tech deep-dive and pre-prod benchmark (due 2026-12-28)
Tom O'Neill: Provide current VPC CIDR, egress list, and firewall owners (due 2026-12-23)
Rhea Kapoor: Send SOC2 and encryption baseline questions; confirm KMS provider (due 2026-12-27)
next_steps: Redwood to send network diagram and recommended subnet layout
Customer to confirm preferred KMS (AWS KMS vs customer HSM)
Agree pilot success criteria and test prompt set
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ramirez (Redwood SE), Nora Patel (Redwood CSM); Maya Green (Prairie VP Eng), Tom O'Neill (Platform Eng), Rhea Kapoor (Security), Samir Desai (DevOps)

Auto-summary (auto): Quick orientation, network intake, security checklist review, pilot next steps.

[00:00] Avery Chen: All right, thanks everybody for joining, um this is Avery from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. We wanted to use today to align on activation runway and the VPC/networking intake. How's everyone doing?

[00:12] Maya Green: Doing good, thanks. We just wrapped up a sprint so timing is good. I pulled Tom and Rhea in to cover network and security.

[00:20] Tom O'Neill: Hey all. Quick note, we're aiming to have staging ready by Jan 10th, but need to lock networking before then.

[00:28] Luis Ramirez: Perfect. I can go through our typical VPC peering and port flow, and then we can map to your infra. One factual note up front — Redwood supports hosted, dedicated, and private VPC deployments. For compliance you mentioned private—correct?

[00:44] Rhea Kapoor: Yes private is preferred. We need audit logs, KMS integration, and preferably no egress to unknown public endpoints.

[00:52] Avery Chen: Totally, that's a common ask. We'll add the audit/log retention details and explain our KMS options. For the pilot we usually recommend a short window with sample traffic to validate latencies and quality.

[01:05] Samir Desai: Quick question — how does Redwood handle fallbacks? Suppose the private cluster is saturated, do you have a hosted fallback that respects our data controls?

[01:16] Luis Ramirez: Yeah so we have routing policies. You can set tiered routing: first attempt private pool, then dedicated reserved, then hosted regional pool. Fallback can be configured to strip PII and only use sanitized prompts if you allow hosted. There's also an option to route to a read-only hosted model for lower-sensitivity tasks.

[01:37] Maya Green: Do we need to sign additional contracts for fallback? We want to keep legal from the back-and forth.

[01:44] Avery Chen: Good call — we'll include clear language in the pilot terms: what data, what models, and whether fallback is allowed. Nora from our CS team will loop in legal and draft the PS addendum if needed.

[01:56] Tom O'Neill: On the network side, our infra team uses strict egress rules, we whitelist destinations. Can you provide the IP ranges and FQDNs?

[02:06] Luis Ramirez: Yes, we'll send the recommended subnet ranges and outbound IPs. Note that some of our telemetry and observability endpoints are hosted; if you want full air-gap we'll discuss a different on-prem packaging but that adds lead time.

[02:22] Rhea Kapoor: When you say on-prem packaging, do you mean a box we host or a customer-managed cluster?

[02:29] Luis Ramirez: Usually customer-managed cluster or appliance-style bundle depending on scale. For regulated workloads we often ship a private control plane and customer-managed compute so logs and keys never leave the environment.

[02:43] Samir Desai: That would be ideal, but curious about monitoring: we still need observability — will the Redwood console be accessible?

[02:51] Nora Patel: You can get console access via private links and we can push metrics to your Prometheus/Grafana. We also support sending structured traces to your S3 or secure bucket.

[03:04] Maya Green: KMS — we use AWS KMS but interested in bringing our HSM later. Is that supported?

[03:11] Luis Ramirez: Yes AWS KMS is supported natively. HSM integrations are possible but require an engineering intake. We'll note that as a longer lead item.

[03:20] Tom O'Neill: For the pilot, what's the minimum support we'd need? GPUs / capacity? We plan to test a 5 concurrent user chat bot and some batch embedding jobs.

[03:31] Luis Ramirez: For that workload we recommend a small dedicated pool or private instance with burst capacity. We'll size it as part of the pilot scoping — usually a few V100/RTX-class instances depending on model choice. We'll propose options in the pilot pricing.

[03:47] Samir Desai: And what about tokenization / prompt costs? We need cost predictability.

[03:53] Avery Chen: We'll share estimated unit economics based on the sample prompt set you give us. For initial planning we'll give you a mid-range and a high-range scenario.

[04:03] Maya Green: One more from me — latency SLO. We need 90th percentile under 350ms for short chat flows. Can you achieve that from our region?

[04:12] Luis Ramirez: Likely yes for the private pool if we co-locate or reserve capacity in your region. We'll validate in benchmarking. If latency is strict, caching of common prefixes and KV cache warming helps a lot.

[04:26] Tom O'Neill: On the security checklist, can you confirm SOC2 type II status and provide our security questionnaire answers?

[04:34] Nora Patel: We're SOC 2 audited — we'll attach the report and an answer matrix. Also can share our access control patterns: RBAC, SSO via SAML/OIDC, and audit log retention options.

[04:46] Rhea Kapoor: Please include API keys rotation cadence and whether Redwood supports hardware-based key wrapping.

[04:52] Luis Ramirez: Short answer — key rotation is supported and you can bring your own KMS. HSM or key wrapping we'll have to detail in the security intake; possible but will require the SEC/infra engineering follow-up.

[05:04] Maya Green: Great. Let's talk timeline — we want staging ready by Jan 10; production by Feb 1 if all goes well. Is that realistic?

[05:12] Avery Chen: Yes that aligns with our standard activation runway. Proposed milestones: network intake (this week), pilot config and pricing (by 12/24), tech deep dive and bench (12/28), pilot run in staging (first two weeks of Jan), go/no-go and production cutover late Jan.

[05:29] Samir Desai: Sounds good. Who owns the runbook?

[05:33] Nora Patel: Redwood will provide a runbook draft, your SRE will review and we will finalize. We'll include rollback steps and monitoring thresholds.

[05:41] Tom O'Neill: I can share our VPC CIDR and firewall contacts after this meeting — I'll drop that in the thread.

[05:47] Maya Green: Also, can you provide a sample prompt set and a list of evaluation metrics you use? We want to align on quality gates.

[05:55] Luis Ramirez: We'll send a prompt set template and recommended eval metrics: response accuracy, hallucination rate, latency percentiles, and token cost per session.

[06:08] Rhea Kapoor: One last quick on data residency — we must ensure EU data stays in EU region for certain customers. Is geo-routing supported?

[06:16] Luis Ramirez: Yes, policy-based routing by region is supported. We'll include region pinning in the rollout policy.

[06:24] Avery Chen: Ok wrapping up — recap and next steps.

[06:29] Avery Chen: Action items: I'll send activation runbook and pricing by 12/24. Luis will schedule tech deep dive for 12/28 and run benchmark. Tom will share VPC details by 12/23. Rhea will compile security Qs by 12/27.

[06:45] Maya Green: That works — thanks everyone.

[06:48] Samir Desai: Thanks, talk soon.

[06:50] Meeting ends.
